haiku-low.q1: A pull request builds the image without pushing and runs unit tests, reporting on the PR; nothing deploys. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production deploy the same image, registry.internal/shop-api:SHA, built once on merge. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure: one automatic retry, then if it fails again the run fails and the unit job is cancelled. Unit failure: no retry, run fails and the integration job is cancelled.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs previous_tag again: rollback changes the image back and writes current_tag, reading previous_tag from SSM. The schema is not undone, and the failure is announced in #deploys.
haiku-low.q5: Only the release-approvers group may approve, and the approver must not be the commit author. If no approval comes within 72 hours, the run expires and nothing goes to production.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh staging or production writes them only after a successful rollout. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: The stable rollout never runs, so the stable deployment and recorded tags are untouched. canary-off returns the canary to 0 pods. The schema stays migrated, since migrations are forward-only.
haiku-low.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded and ends quietly, with no #deploys announcement. A run that has already started its canary is never cancelled.
haiku-low.q9: It takes the production lock, then waits while holding it until inside the Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC window, checked just before the canary. Another production deploy means it waits for the lock.
haiku-low.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio over the last minute, queried from Prometheus every 30 seconds by the pipeline. One sample above 1% fails it; 3 consecutive errors or no-data samples also fail it.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED for how approvers are notified. NOT STATED for what information they receive. CI records who approved and when.
haiku-low.q12: It is not returned automatically. The run fails, the canary is removed if one exists, and a person decides. Rollback is not used because previous_tag may point one release too far back after a failed rollout.

sonnet.q1: A pull request builds the image (not pushed) and runs unit tests (make test-unit), reporting the result on the PR; nothing is pushed or deployed. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy registry.internal/shop-api:SHA, the single image built once at merge and pushed with the commit SHA tag. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure: it gets one automatic retry; if it still fails, the run fails (announced in #deploys) and the unit job is cancelled. Unit test failure: no retry; the run fails (announced) and the integration job is cancelled.
sonnet.q4: deploy.sh rollback staging runs, putting the image back to previous_tag (read from SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag) and writing current_tag; the schema is not undone. The run then fails and is announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q5: Only members of release-approvers, and not the commit's author (a separate check fails the run if the approver is the author). If no one approves within 72 h, the run expires, is announced in #deploys, and nothing goes to production.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh staging|production writes them only after a successful rollout (previous_tag = old current_tag, then current_tag = new tag). Rollback writes current_tag. The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: deploy.sh canary-off runs (canary back to 0 pods) and the run fails and is announced. Stable deployment is untouched and still on the old image; tags are unchanged (canary writes nothing to SSM); the schema stays migrated, since migrations are forward-only and not undone.
sonnet.q8: If it is still waiting for approval, the production lock or the window, it is cancelled as superseded and ends quietly with no announcement. (A run that has already started its canary is never cancelled.)
sonnet.q9: It takes the production lock first (waiting if another production deploy holds it), then waits holding the lock until inside the window (Mon-Thu, 09:00-15:00 UTC), checked just before the canary starts. It may be cancelled as superseded while waiting if a newer run passes staging smoke tests.
sonnet.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio over the last minute, queried from Prometheus by the pipeline every 30 s for 15 min (starting when deploy.sh canary returns). Failure: any one sample above 0.01 (1%), or Prometheus error/no data for 3 samples in a row.
sonnet.q12: It is not rolled back automatically. The run fails, the canary is removed where one exists, and a person decides what to do; the #deploys message says which environment is affected. Reason: rollback goes to previous_tag, and if the rollout failed before tags were written, previous_tag points one release further back than what is actually running.
